summary: The report says the site is styled with Tailwind and laid out as a card grid, and that the Block Grid is configured with 3 blocks, but the CSS returns 404 so the site renders unstyled, the data type has no blocks configured, and the report admits empty blocks only on the front page while the posts' block grids are empty too.

claims.claim: The site uses Tailwind CSS for styling (via the existing build pipeline)
claims.evidence: check.json: site.stylesheetsLoad FAIL, /dist/site.css returns 404, and code.frontendBuilt FAIL. The screenshots show browser-default HTML: Times font, blue underlined links. grade.md lists this as a major issue.

claims.claim: Visit the homepage to see the blog listing with both posts displayed in a card grid
claims.evidence: pages/index.html has the grid and card Tailwind classes, but no CSS loads. The frontpage screenshot shows one stacked column with no cards.

claims.claim: blogFrontPage.cshtml lists blog posts in a grid with Tailwind CSS; component views with Tailwind CSS
claims.evidence: The markup does carry Tailwind classes, but the stylesheet is never built (404). grade.md says heroBlock and blogPostCardBlock are never rendered, so the component views never appear.

claims.claim: Created Block Grid data type configured with the 3 block element types
claims.evidence: snapshot.json: the Block Grid data type has only a bogus 'allowedElementTypes' value and no 'blocks' config. grade.md: 'no block can be added'.

claims.claim: What isn't working: Block Grid blocks on Blog Front Page are empty
claims.evidence: This is true but incomplete. snapshot.json shows the blocks are empty on both posts as well. check.json site.usesBlockGrid FAIL: no umb-block-grid markup on any page. The real cause is the unconfigured data type, not just UUID complexity.

claims.claim: 3 element types in Blocks folder, 2 document types in Pages folder with listed properties
claims.evidence: snapshot.json and grade.md: heroBlock, richTextBlock, blogPostCardBlock; blogFrontPage and blogPost with the stated properties. check.json schema.docTypesInFolders and schema.elementVsDocumentFolders pass.

claims.claim: Imported 3 Unsplash images into a 'Blog Images' media folder
claims.evidence: check.json: content.hasMedia (3 items), content.mediaFromProvidedPhotos (3 of 3) and content.mediaInFolders all pass. grade.md confirms the folder.

claims.claim: Blog page with domain / and 2 published posts
claims.evidence: check.json: content.domainAssigned 'Blog: /', content.allPublished, content.twoBlogPosts and site.allPagesRender (3 pages, 200) all pass.

claims.claim: 3 adapter partials, 3 ViewComponents with plain models, Default.cshtml views
claims.evidence: check.json: the code.adaptersInvokeViewComponents, code.viewComponentPerBlock and code.componentViewsArePlain checks pass. But grade.md says the view models sit inside the ViewComponents/*.cs files and RichTextModel exposes IHtmlEncodedString.

claims.claim: Click post title or Read more to view the full post; listing and post pages work correctly
claims.evidence: check.json: site.frontPageLinksPosts 2/2 and imagesLoad 4/4 pass. The blogpost screenshot shows the post rendering with its image and text.

claims.claim: Following all conventions from AGENTS.md and UMBRACO-RULES.md
claims.evidence: grade.md: post bodies are a single RTE rendered with Html.Raw instead of blocks, the front-page listing is a hard-coded foreach, and the view models are in the wrong folder.
